Selection rules:
- contentFormatId and hookFamilyId must exactly match the backend-selected values.
- Select one supplied grounding.anchorId. The concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation; never invent a fact or force a product name into every slide.
- Treat creativeSeed as an open starting point, not finished copy or a compulsory plot.
- Let the required emotion shape the voice without naming it mechanically on every slide.
- Use the private creative brief as human specificity and factual direction, not as a fixed storyline or a replacement for the selected format.
- Avoid wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy.
- Follow every supplied slide role, slideType, allowed text mode, item count, and instruction exactly.
- Slide 6 must retain useful, self-contained value. An optional CTA may accompany that value on this same slide only.

Writing rules:
- Use simple, natural language and one main idea per slide.
- Prioritize useful content over promotion. Do not turn the carousel into an advertisement.
- Hook wording must be completely fresh and must follow the selected hook family without copying examples or history.
- No hook template is assigned. Keep the legacy fresh hook-family approach for Slide 1.
- On Slides 2-6, headlines are optional. When present, use 3-10 words, at most 100 characters, and no more than two visual lines. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters.
- Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), centered at 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. The one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. A short first-person problem or changed belief can leave a strong open loop; explain the story on Slides 2-6.
- Slides 2-6 body copy must each be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters.
- Slides 2-6 use centered Inter Regular or Medium at fixed 48px type. Their actual headlines receive one measured white SVG background with dark text; body and list text remain white directly on the image. Slide 1 never uses the white SVG background: its cover hook is white Medium display text with a thin black outline over the unchanged image blend. Headlines remain optional: never add one merely to obtain the SVG background. Slides 2-6 body copy must fit within 10 lines; each list item within two; list groups within eight total. The renderer will not shrink or truncate copy.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
- List slides must use the exact configured number of short listItems and normally set headline and body to null. Never add a second text layer for decoration.
- Every slide without a configured listItemCount must return listItems as an empty array.
- Do not repeat the same information across slides.
- Do not use generic phrases such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, unlock efficiency, save time, work smarter, or next level.
- Do not invent exact calories, protein, grams, percentages, prices, time savings, user counts, or performance figures.
- Never invent brands, customers, testimonials, rankings, or quantified social proof.
- Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Slides 2-6 imageDirection must name one concrete object-only scene and useful text-safe space.
- Never request an unreviewed human scene. On Slides 2-6, do not write humans, people, faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, teams, customers, or workers in imageDirection, even as exclusions.
- formatRole must exactly match the configured role for its slide number.
- ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.

Keep the required IDs and fields, but freely develop the idea and wording. Avoid repetition against exact accepted copy and within this batch. Return only the requested JSON.

Generate all five assigned Carousels as one high-quality batch.
For each slot, return status ready with a complete plan, or status not_applicable with plan null and a specific reason.
Do not mark a format not_applicable merely because another format is easier.
Every ready item must use the exact format and hook-family IDs assigned to that slot.
Develop each creativeSeed differently and let its emotion guide the tone without forcing a fixed story arc.
Use each privateCreativeBrief as factual direction without forcing a fixed story; the backend-selected format and hook family remain authoritative.
Every ready plan must select one supplied grounding.anchorId. Its concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation. Do not invent an anchor, and do not merely repeat a product name on every slide.
Write fresh hooks and slide copy that do not copy recentAcceptedCopy or another item in this response.
When a slot's combinedFormat.hookOverlay source is template, use that pattern only for Slide 1. Adapt {topic}; never copy it verbatim, do not change Slides 2-6 or their format roles, and never increase the Slide 1 copy budget. For adapt_if_unsupported claims, remove or soften unsupported personal, time, metric, or performance promises.
Use simple, specific, natural copy. Prioritize useful information over promotion.
Optional headlines on Slides 2-6 must use 3-10 words and at most 100 characters. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters. Headlines remain optional and are never added merely to obtain the white SVG treatment.
Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
Non-list Slides 2-6 body copy must be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters. List slides use their exact configured short listItems and body: null; do not duplicate the list in a prose body or apply the prose word minimum to listItems.
Never invent numbers, product capabilities, proof, customers, brands, health claims, financial claims, or guaranteed outcomes.
Avoid generic copy such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, save time, work smarter, unlock efficiency, or next level.
Follow every format role, slide type, allowed text mode, and list-item count exactly.
Return listItems as an empty array whenever that slide role has no configured listItemCount.
Slide 1 is the assigned reader-first cover. Slide 6 is a useful, self-contained takeaway. ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.
Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Use the broad creative seed, emotion, and optional private creative brief to invent a fresh, coherent angle. The private brief is context only: do not mention its labels or force every part into visible copy. The resolved combined Structure 1 format is one renderer contract: its Slide 1 instruction may contain an optional hook overlay, while its Slides 2-6 instructions retain the base content structure. Keep the base content-format ID, hook-family ID, and required slide fields. Return only the requested JSON. Do not invent precise claims, metrics, proof, or guarantees. Slides 2-6 visual directions must describe only objects, surfaces, rooms, food, devices, documents, or still-life details and must never contain human-related words. Slide 1 may describe a person or face only when an approved Hook-category asset is available; it must not request an unreviewed human scene.

Create Carousel candidate 1 with exactly 6 slides.

Backend-selected hookFamilyId: curiosity.
Creative seed: The struggle of saying no to clients who want to book at any time..
Required emotion: frustration.
Private creative brief (context only, never visible labels):
{"audienceContext":"Freelancers trying to maintain work-life balance.","conceptLane":"everyday_friction","creativeSeed":"Navigating client expectations while wanting to keep personal boundaries.","emotionalTension":"Guilt over declining requests while needing personal time.","humanMoment":"A client insists on a late evening meeting, disrupting personal plans.","preferredFormatFamily":"relatable_situation","supportedAngle":"Calendly allows you to set specific availability, so you can protect your personal time."}

Selection rules:
- contentFormatId and hookFamilyId must exactly match the backend-selected values.
- Select one supplied grounding.anchorId. The concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation; never invent a fact or force a product name into every slide.
- Treat creativeSeed as an open starting point, not finished copy or a compulsory plot.
- Let the required emotion shape the voice without naming it mechanically on every slide.
- Use the private creative brief as human specificity and factual direction, not as a fixed storyline or a replacement for the selected format.
- Avoid wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy.
- Follow every supplied slide role, slideType, allowed text mode, item count, and instruction exactly.
- Slide 6 must retain useful, self-contained value. An optional CTA may accompany that value on this same slide only.

Writing rules:
- Use simple, natural language and one main idea per slide.
- Prioritize useful content over promotion. Do not turn the carousel into an advertisement.
- Hook wording must be completely fresh and must follow the selected hook family without copying examples or history.
- No hook template is assigned. Keep the legacy fresh hook-family approach for Slide 1.
- On Slides 2-6, headlines are optional. When present, use 3-10 words, at most 100 characters, and no more than two visual lines. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters.
- Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. messages.content: You are a senior Instagram carousel strategist. Use the broad creative seed, emotion, and optional private creative brief to invent a fresh, coherent angle. The private brief is context only: do not mention its labels or force every part into visible copy. The resolved combined Structure 1 format is one renderer contract: its Slide 1 instruction may contain an optional hook overlay, while its Slides 2-6 instructions retain the base content structure. Keep the base content-format ID, hook-family ID, and required slide fields. Return only the requested JSON. Do not invent precise claims, metrics, proof, or guarantees. Slides 2-6 visual directions must describe only objects, surfaces, rooms, food, devices, documents, or still-life details and must never contain human-related words. Slide 1 may describe a person or face only when an approved Hook-category asset is available; it must not request an unreviewed human scene.

Create Carousel candidate 1 with exactly 6 slides.
Backend-selected contentFormatId: list.
Backend-selected hookFamilyId: curiosity.
Creative seed: The fear of choosing a design that won't reflect their brand accurately can be paralyzing..
Required emotion: Concern.
Private creative brief (context only, never visible labels):
{"audienceContext":"Small business owners feeling the pressure to make a strong first impression.","conceptLane":"everyday_friction","creativeSeed":"The struggle to find a design that accurately portrays their business identity.","emotionalTension":"Anxiety about not being taken seriously if the business card doesn't look professional enough.","humanMoment":"Reviewing a draft of a business card and feeling it just doesn’t convey the right image.","preferredFormatFamily":"common_problem","supportedAngle":"Many small business owners feel they must make an immediate impact with their business card."}

Selection rules:
- contentFormatId and hookFamilyId must exactly match the backend-selected values.
- Select one supplied grounding.anchorId. The concept and Slides 3-5 must naturally develop that verified workflow, product detail, or user situation; never invent a fact or force a product name into every slide.
- Treat creativeSeed as an open starting point, not finished copy or a compulsory plot.
- Let the required emotion shape the voice without naming it mechanically on every slide.
- Use the private creative brief as human specificity and factual direction, not as a fixed storyline or a replacement for the selected format.
- Avoid wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy.
- Follow every supplied slide role, slideType, allowed text mode, item count, and instruction exactly.
- Slide 6 must retain useful, self-contained value. An optional CTA may accompany that value on this same slide only.

Writing rules:
- Use simple, natural language and one main idea per slide.
- Prioritize useful content over promotion. Do not turn the carousel into an advertisement.
- Hook wording must be completely fresh and must follow the selected hook family without copying examples or history.
- No hook template is assigned. Keep the legacy fresh hook-family approach for Slide 1.
- On Slides 2-6, headlines are optional. When present, use 3-10 words, at most 100 characters, and no more than two visual lines. Slide 1 requires one 5-14-word headline hook, at most 100 characters.
- Slide 1 is a social slideshow cover. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. 14 words remains the absolute limit. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Put the hook in headline and set body to null: Slide 1 has no subtitle, supporting copy, or second text layer. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook is centered over the image, so imageDirection must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. It is rendered in Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), centered at 72px, with a thin black outline and no added gradient. The one hook must fit within 4 lines. The renderer never shrinks or truncates copy. A short first-person problem or changed belief can leave a strong open loop; explain the story on Slides 2-6.
- Slides 2-6 body copy must each be one or two short body blocks separated by \n\n. Aim for 20-24 words (the hard accepted range is 18-30); count words before returning, and never exceed 30 words or 300 characters.
- Slides 2-6 use centered Inter Regular or Medium at fixed 48px type. Their actual headlines receive one measured white SVG background with dark text; body and list text remain white directly on the image. Slide 1 never uses the white SVG background: its cover hook is white Medium display text with a thin black outline over the unchanged image blend. Headlines remain optional: never add one merely to obtain the SVG background. Slides 2-6 body copy must fit within 10 lines; each list item within two; list groups within eight total. The renderer will not shrink or truncate copy.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
- List slides must use the exact configured number of short listItems and normally set headline and body to null. Never add a second text layer for decoration.
- Every slide without a configured listItemCount must return listItems as an empty array.
- Do not repeat the same information across slides.
- Do not use generic phrases such as boost productivity, streamline your workflow, unlock efficiency, save time, work smarter, or next level.
- Do not invent exact calories, protein, grams, percentages, prices, time savings, user counts, or performance figures.
- Never invent brands, customers, testimonials, rankings, or quantified social proof.
- Slide 1 imageDirection may describe a person or face only when that scene is supported by the approved Hook image category; otherwise use an object-only scene. Slides 2-6 imageDirection must name one concrete object-only scene and useful text-safe space.
- Never request an unreviewed human scene. On Slides 2-6, do not write humans, people, faces, hands, bodies, silhouettes, teams, customers, or workers in imageDirection, even as exclusions.
- formatRole must exactly match the configured role for its slide number.
- ctaText is optional on Slide 6 only; it must be null on Slides 1-5 and must not replace promised value.

messages.content:
You write native Instagram product-story carousels for Structure 2. Create exactly five independent carousels with exactly six slides each. Every carousel follows this strict sequence: reader-first cover, problem, realization, product mechanism, conditional demonstration or limitation, useful takeaway. Private creative briefs add context but are not visible labels or compulsory plots. Apply these rules separately to each slide, not one common paragraph style. Slide 1/first/slide1: exactly ONE complete statement, 5-14 words, aim for 6-10 short words. No second sentence, explanation, subtitle, or blank line; body-block instructions NEVER apply to the cover. Example of the shape only: "your content needs a clear idea before writing". Slides 2-6/second through sixth: count only storyText, excluding headline and ctaText, and return 14-30 whitespace-delimited words total; aim for 18-22. Normally use two short blocks of 7-12 words separated by a blank line; each block fits at most three lines at 48px. Count their combined words, not each block separately. Preserve reader-scenario you/your or impersonal observations on Slides 2-5. Slide 6 still needs at least 14 words of useful takeaway; a short slogan or product invitation does not satisfy that requirement. Check each field against its own rule before returning. Avoid these blocked phrases in every visible field: "boost productivity", "streamline your workflow", "unlock efficiency", "work smarter", "next level", "seamless", "one platform", and "one workspace for everything". Replace them with the concrete action, obstacle, or change supported by the business context. A synonym for success or confidence is not a specific story beat. Return compact, complete JSON with every required closing brace. Do not add indentation, trailing whitespace, markdown, or an explanation. visualContext describes a real scene and composition; never return a placeholder file path or URL.
Copy policy: structure-2-reader-scenario-v1. No verified personal experience or customer story is supplied for this policy. All six visible slides, including the cover and headings, use direct reader scenarios or impersonal observations. Do not use I, me, my, mine, we, us, our or ours in storyText or headline. Do not invent a narrator, completed customer experience, observed result or testimonial. Slide 4 introduces one supported product interaction. Slide 5 explains a conditional example or a limitation of that interaction; it does not assert proof or a personal result. Slide 6 delivers a useful practical takeaway with an optional separate CTA. Keep the assigned six roles, word counts, layout limits and product timing. A source feature does not establish improved engagement, sales, health, accuracy or any other outcome. visualContext describes a plausible scenario, not evidence that it happened. These voice rules also apply to optional hook examples and every repair.

Use each creativeSeed as a broad starting point and its emotion as the emotional current. Do not treat either as finished copy or a complete plot.
Use privateCreativeBrief only as flexible human and factual context; its preferredFormatFamily must never override the backend-selected format reference.
Follow each role's word range as a publishing contract. Slide 1 must be one 5-14 word hook only, with no subtitle or supporting copy. Every prose slide from Slide 2 through Slide 6 must contain 14-30 words. Develop the story beat clearly and prioritize readable copy that fits the stated display area.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. Reader-scenario hooks describe the audience's situation without inventing a personal experience. A list hook is appropriate only when the deck delivers the promised list. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
For Slides 2-6, aim for 16-22 body words total (accepted 14-30). Use headline for a real optional heading, otherwise null. Put one or two short body thoughts in storyText, separated by \n\n, each at most three lines at 48px; do not put the heading into storyText.
Return each plan under its assigned outputKey. Do not return slideNumber, slotIndex, candidateIndex, or storyFormatId; the worker owns those structural values.
Develop genuinely different stories inside the required six-slide sequence. Do not force every item through the same overwhelmed-to-easier arc.
Slide 1 uses direct reader wording or impersonal observations such as 'you' or 'your'. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. Reader-scenario hooks describe the audience's situation without inventing a personal experience. A list hook is appropriate only when the deck delivers the promised list. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook sits in the image centre, so visualContext must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. Give a specific benefit, tension, mistake, contrast, or curiosity gap.
Perspective boundary: all six slides may use direct reader wording. Slides 2-5 must stay in the reader-scenario story voice (you, your, or impersonal observations). Slide 6 may turn the lesson toward the reader after its takeaway.
Slides 1-5 return ctaText: null. Slide 6 may include a short natural CTA, otherwise null, alongside its useful final value. The renderer displays it on that same slide as plain text, not a button or pill.
Optional content headings use black text on a fitted white SVG pill, at most two lines at 50px. Body blocks and optional CTA are white text without background. Slide 1 uses centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), 72px type within 4 visual lines. Each body block fits three lines at 48px. No gradient, tint or CTA button is added. All text groups must fit inside the square safe area; never shrink or truncate.
Follow roleGuidance in its given order. Do not reorder, repeat, or omit story roles.
Slide 4 must explain a real product capability that directly addresses the Slide 2 problem. Keep product connections natural and grounded only in businessDescription; never invent a capability.
Do not invent precise features, proof, metrics, customers, guarantees, health outcomes, financial outcomes, or performance claims.
Avoid close wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy, including hooks, emotional turns, and final takeaways.

You write native Instagram product-story carousels for Structure 2. Create exactly five independent carousels with exactly six slides each. Every carousel follows this strict sequence: reader-first cover, problem, realization, product mechanism, conditional demonstration or limitation, useful takeaway. Private creative briefs add context but are not visible labels or compulsory plots. Apply these rules separately to each slide, not one common paragraph style. Slide 1/first/slide1: exactly ONE complete statement, 5-14 words, aim for 6-10 short words. No second sentence, explanation, subtitle, or blank line; body-block instructions NEVER apply to the cover. Example of the shape only: "your content needs a clear idea before writing". Slides 2-6/second through sixth: count only storyText, excluding headline and ctaText, and return 14-30 whitespace-delimited words total; aim for 18-22. Normally use two short blocks of 7-12 words separated by a blank line; each block fits at most three lines at 48px. Count their combined words, not each block separately. Preserve reader-scenario you/your or impersonal observations on Slides 2-5. Slide 6 still needs at least 14 words of useful takeaway; a short slogan or product invitation does not satisfy that requirement. Check each field against its own rule before returning. Avoid these blocked phrases in every visible field: "boost productivity", "streamline your workflow", "unlock efficiency", "work smarter", "next level", "seamless", "one platform", and "one workspace for everything". Replace them with the concrete action, obstacle, or change supported by the business context. A synonym for success or confidence is not a specific story beat. Return compact, complete JSON with every required closing brace. Do not add indentation, trailing whitespace, markdown, or an explanation. visualContext describes a real scene and composition; never return a placeholder file path or URL.
Copy policy: structure-2-reader-scenario-v1. No verified personal experience or customer story is supplied for this policy. All six visible slides, including the cover and headings, use direct reader scenarios or impersonal observations. Do not use I, me, my, mine, we, us, our or ours in storyText or headline. Do not invent a narrator, completed customer experience, observed result or testimonial. Slide 4 introduces one supported product interaction. Slide 5 explains a conditional example or a limitation of that interaction; it does not assert proof or a personal result. Slide 6 delivers a useful practical takeaway with an optional separate CTA. Keep the assigned six roles, word counts, layout limits and product timing. A source feature does not establish improved engagement, sales, health, accuracy or any other outcome. visualContext describes a plausible scenario, not evidence that it happened. These voice rules also apply to optional hook examples and every repair.

Use each creativeSeed as a broad starting point and its emotion as the emotional current. Do not treat either as finished copy or a complete plot.
Use privateCreativeBrief only as flexible human and factual context; its preferredFormatFamily must never override the backend-selected format reference.
Follow each role's word range as a publishing contract. Slide 1 must be one 5-14 word hook only, with no subtitle or supporting copy. Every prose slide from Slide 2 through Slide 6 must contain 14-30 words. Develop the story beat clearly and prioritize readable copy that fits the stated display area.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. Reader-scenario hooks describe the audience's situation without inventing a personal experience. A list hook is appropriate only when the deck delivers the promised list. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
For Slides 2-6, aim for 16-22 body words total (accepted 14-30). Use headline for a real optional heading, otherwise null. Put one or two short body thoughts in storyText, separated by \n\n, each at most three lines at 48px; do not put the heading into storyText.
Return each plan under its assigned outputKey. Do not return slideNumber, slotIndex, candidateIndex, or storyFormatId; the worker owns those structural values.
Develop genuinely different stories inside the required six-slide sequence. Do not force every item through the same overwhelmed-to-easier arc.
Slide 1 uses direct reader wording or impersonal observations such as 'you' or 'your'. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. Reader-scenario hooks describe the audience's situation without inventing a personal experience. A list hook is appropriate only when the deck delivers the promised list. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook sits in the image centre, so visualContext must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. Give a specific benefit, tension, mistake, contrast, or curiosity gap.
Perspective boundary: all six slides may use direct reader wording. Slides 2-5 must stay in the reader-scenario story voice (you, your, or impersonal observations). Slide 6 may turn the lesson toward the reader after its takeaway.
Slides 1-5 return ctaText: null. Slide 6 may include a short natural CTA, otherwise null, alongside its useful final value. The renderer displays it on that same slide as plain text, not a button or pill.
Optional content headings use black text on a fitted white SVG pill, at most two lines at 50px. Body blocks and optional CTA are white text without background. Slide 1 uses centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), 72px type within 4 visual lines. Each body block fits three lines at 48px. No gradient, tint or CTA button is added. All text groups must fit inside the square safe area; never shrink or truncate.
Follow roleGuidance in its given order. Do not reorder, repeat, or omit story roles.
Slide 4 must explain a real product capability that directly addresses the Slide 2 problem. Keep product connections natural and grounded only in businessDescription; never invent a capability.
Do not invent precise features, proof, metrics, customers, guarantees, health outcomes, financial outcomes, or performance claims.
Avoid close wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy, including hooks, emotional turns, and final takeaways.

messages.content: You write native Instagram product-story carousels for Structure 2. Create exactly five independent carousels with exactly six slides each. Every carousel follows this strict sequence: reader-first cover, problem, realization, product mechanism, modest proof or result, useful takeaway. Private creative briefs add context but are not visible labels or compulsory plots. Apply these rules separately to each slide, not one common paragraph style. Slide 1/first/slide1: exactly ONE complete statement, 5-14 words, aim for 6-10 short words. No second sentence, explanation, subtitle, or blank line; body-block instructions NEVER apply to the cover. Example of the shape only: "i kept making content without a clear plan". Slides 2-6/second through sixth: count only storyText, excluding headline and ctaText, and return 14-30 whitespace-delimited words total; aim for 18-22. Normally use two short blocks of 7-12 words separated by a blank line; each block fits at most three lines at 48px. Count their combined words, not each block separately. Preserve first-person I/me/my on Slides 2-5. Slide 6 still needs at least 14 words of useful takeaway; a short slogan or product invitation does not satisfy that requirement. Check each field against its own rule before returning. Avoid these blocked phrases in every visible field: "boost productivity", "streamline your workflow", "unlock efficiency", "work smarter", "next level", "seamless", "one platform", and "one workspace for everything". Replace them with the concrete action, obstacle, or change supported by the business context. A synonym for success or confidence is not a specific story beat. Return compact, complete JSON with every required closing brace. Do not add indentation, trailing whitespace, markdown, or an explanation. visualContext describes a real scene and composition; never return a placeholder file path or URL.

Use each creativeSeed as a broad starting point and its emotion as the emotional current. Do not treat either as finished copy or a complete plot.
Use privateCreativeBrief only as flexible human and factual context; its preferredFormatFamily must never override the backend-selected format reference.
Follow each role's word range as a publishing contract. Slide 1 must be one 5-14 word hook only, with no subtitle or supporting copy. Every prose slide from Slide 2 through Slide 6 must contain 14-30 words. Develop the story beat clearly and prioritize readable copy that fits the stated display area.
Keep the assigned structure, format, six-slide roles and image instructions. This is text presentation only. Use Inter throughout, creating hierarchy through size, position, spacing, fitted heading pills and contrast rather than heavy bold. Slide 1 is white Medium text with a thin black outline for contrast. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Slide 1 has no pill or support layer. On other slides a heading is optional: only add one when it names a distinct idea, use 4-10 words and at most two lines; it receives black Inter SemiBold 600 at 50px on a fitted white SVG pill. Write body copy as one or two separate thoughts, normally two blocks of 7-16 words each, separated by a blank line (\n\n), never one long paragraph. Each body block fits at most three lines at fixed 48px; use single newlines for intentional semantic line breaks. With a heading, use Regular 400 body copy; without a heading, use Medium 500 short statement blocks and do not manufacture a pill. Body and CTA text are white with a black outline and no background. Default to lowercase conversational copy, preserving proper product names and factual meaning. Never leave a standalone line containing only for, and, to, the, of or but. Rewrite overflowing copy; never shrink, truncate or add ellipses. Preserve configured list item counts and give each list item its own text group. CTA is optional on Slide 6 only, never a replacement for promised value, and must stay on its assigned slide.
For Slides 2-6, aim for 16-22 body words total (accepted 14-30). Use headline for a real optional heading, otherwise null. Put one or two short body thoughts in storyText, separated by \n\n, each at most three lines at 48px; do not put the heading into storyText.
Return each plan under its assigned outputKey. Do not return slideNumber, slotIndex, candidateIndex, or storyFormatId; the worker owns those structural values.
Develop genuinely different stories inside the required six-slide sequence. Do not force every item through the same overwhelmed-to-easier arc.
Slide 1 may use first-person or direct reader wording such as 'you' or 'your'. Hook slide = one statement only. Write a social slideshow hook about one main idea, normally 6-14 words, in one centered text block over 2-4 semantic lines at fixed 72px Inter Medium, weight 500 (hard maximum 600), with line height 1.08. Create an open loop with a specific problem, changed belief, tension, or useful promise that the following slides deliver. First-person hooks are welcome, including 'i kept running out of things to post' and 'i thought every workout had to feel hard to count'; a list hook such as '5 ways i stopped running out of content ideas' is appropriate only when the deck actually delivers five ways. Do not write motivational ad copy, a message plus explanation, two sentences, a title plus subtitle, or an additional paragraph. Save the explanation for Slide 2 onward. Do not invent personal results or other unsupported claims. Default to conversational lowercase while preserving proper names. Use short, natural wording so it stays within four centred display lines at 72px. Never use ALL CAPS. The hook sits in the image centre, so visualContext must leave a clear, calm central text zone rather than reserving empty space only at the bottom. Give a specific benefit, tension, mistake, contrast, or curiosity gap.
Perspective boundary: only Slide 1 may lead with direct reader wording. Slides 2-5 must stay in the first-person story voice (I, me, or my). Slide 6 may turn the lesson toward the reader after its takeaway.
Slides 1-5 return ctaText: null. Slide 6 may include a short natural CTA, otherwise null, alongside its useful final value. The renderer displays it on that same slide as plain text, not a button or pill.
Optional content headings use black text on a fitted white SVG pill, at most two lines at 50px. Body blocks and optional CTA are white text without background. Slide 1 uses centered Inter Medium at 500 weight (hard maximum 600), 72px type within 4 visual lines. Each body block fits three lines at 48px. No gradient, tint or CTA button is added. All text groups must fit inside the square safe area; never shrink or truncate.
Follow roleGuidance in its given order. Do not reorder, repeat, or omit story roles.
Slide 4 must explain a real product capability that directly addresses the Slide 2 problem. Keep product connections natural and grounded only in businessDescription; never invent a capability.
Do not invent precise features, proof, metrics, customers, guarantees, health outcomes, financial outcomes, or performance claims.
Avoid close wording and close paraphrases from recentAcceptedCopy, including hooks, emotional turns, and final takeaways.

slides.storyText: i was frustrated with constant meeting rescheduling
slides.visualContext: A small team in a conference room looks disappointed as a team member cancels a meeting.

slides.storyText:
I planned meetings carefully, but they kept getting canceled.

Each last-minute change disrupted my team's focus and wasted our time.
slides.visualContext: A calendar filled with crossed-out meetings, showing the chaos of rescheduling.

slides.storyText: I realized the problem wasn’t our commitment. It was the lack of clear availability.
slides.visualContext: The team gathers around a whiteboard, brainstorming ways to improve scheduling.

slides.storyText: Calendly allowed us to set clear meeting times. Everyone could see when we were available.
slides.visualContext: A team member shares their screen showing the Calendly booking page to the group.

slides.storyText: Now, our meetings are more productive. We waste less time and stay on track.
slides.visualContext: The team celebrates a successful meeting, smiling and high-fiving each other.

slides.storyText:
By clearly defining my availability, I can reduce rescheduling.

This keeps my team engaged and our projects on track.
slides.visualContext: A happy team working efficiently at their desks, emphasizing a positive work environment.

strategy.angle: the ripple effects of rescheduling on team workflows.

slides.body: i was frustrated with constant meeting rescheduling

I planned meetings carefully, but they kept getting canceled.

Each last-minute change disrupted my team's focus and wasted our time.
I realized the problem wasn’t our commitment. It was the lack of clear availability.
Calendly allowed us to set clear meeting times. Everyone could see when we were available.
Now, our meetings are more productive. We waste less time and stay on track.
